definitions.explanation: A flavorful liquid base used in Japanese cooking, typically made from kombu (kelp), katsuobushi (dried bonito flakes), or both.

examples.notes: 出汁を取る is the standard expression for making/extracting dashi

examples.japanese: {昆布|こんぶ}と{鰹節|かつおぶし}で{出汁|だし}を{作|つく}りました。
examples.english: I made dashi from kelp and dried bonito flakes.

examples.japanese: この{味噌汁|みそしる}は{出汁|だし}が{効|き}いていて{美味|おい}しい。
examples.english: This miso soup tastes good because the dashi flavor comes through well.
examples.notes: 出汁が効く means the dashi flavor is prominent

notes:
Essential in Japanese cuisine. Common types include:
- {昆布|こんぶ}{出汁|だし} (kelp stock)
- {鰹|かつお}{出汁|だし} (bonito stock)
- {合|あ}わせ{出汁|だし} (combination stock)
- {煮干|にぼ}し{出汁|だし} (dried sardine stock)

Also written as だし or ダシ in casual contexts. Instant dashi granules ({顆粒|かりゅう}だし or ほんだし) are widely used for convenience.
